finding_1_rate_is_a_dial: The cumulative 50M gate rate is set by q alone and is width- and seed-invariant: seven q=0.8 runs across an 8x width range and two seeds land inside 0.1978..0.1994 (0.16pp scatter); four q=0.75 runs across two widths and two seeds land inside 0.2466..0.2478 (0.12pp). The 4.9pp 'fall at d512' in the original curve was the q flip, not width. Both q levels are seed-hard (P56c completed).
finding_2_ratio_crossing: At fixed q=0.8 and matched dose the improvement ratio crosses 1.0 at d1024 on BOTH seeds: 1.0092 (seed 42) and 1.0304 (seed 43), mean 1.0198 — the gated arm beats the full-gradient arm outright on ~one fifth of the gradient tokens; the second seed lands above the first. Curve at q=0.8: 0.9708 (d128) -> 0.9841/0.9892 (d256) -> 0.9777/0.9758 (d512) -> 1.0092/1.0304 (d1024). The d512 valley holds on both d256 seeds (P65b). Ratio seed-deltas grow as width shrinks (d512 0.0019, d256 0.0051, d128/q75 0.0078); rates never exceed 0.06pp seed-delta.
finding_3_efficiency_corrected: At fixed q=0.8, improvement per million gradient tokens FALLS monotonically with width (0.3696 -> 0.3629 -> 0.3547/0.3467 -> 0.3305). The old 'efficiency grows with width' read (0.2969/0.2937 -> 0.3547) compared q=0.75 doses against a q=0.8 dose: the higher quantile doses fewer, more selective tokens, which raises per-token improvement regardless of width. P56(a)'s registered bar (d1024 >= 0.3547) reads FAIL, and the pre-committed falsifier fires: the per-token efficiency curve has its maximum before d1024. The width-clean statement is the ratio, and the ratio culminates in the d1024 crossing.
still_open: RESOLVED 2026-08-10: the q=0.75/seed-43 pair completed (0.2466/0.2478) — P56(c) PASS. Remaining refinement: ratio-shape claims below d512 need seed pairs (P65a missed its +-0.005 bar by 0.0001).
anchor_caveat: All points share the 50M-token anchor; A2 degrades with width at fixed tokens (4.93 -> 5.04 -> 5.09/5.14 -> 5.45), so the anchor sits earlier in a wider model's training. Absolute improvements (A1-A3) shrink with width for both arms; the ratio normalizes this, per-token efficiency does not.
